record.title: Nice-group conjecture for cross-indices of face posets
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a **nice group**, meaning a cyclic $p$-group or a generalized quaternion group whose order is a power of $2$. For a finite free $G$-simplicial complex $\mathcal{K}$, let $\mathcal{F}(\mathcal{K})$ be its face poset, and let $\operatorname{x-ind}$ denote the cross-index used in the source. **Nice-group face-poset conjecture.** For every pair $\mathcal{K}_1,\mathcal{K}_2$ of finite free $G$-simplicial complexes,

$$
\operatorname{x-ind}\bigl(\mathcal{F}(\mathcal{K}_1)\times\mathcal{F}(\mathcal{K}_2)\bigr)=\min\{\operatorname{x-ind}\mathcal{F}(\mathcal{K}_1),\operatorname{x-ind}\mathcal{F}(\mathcal{K}_2)\}.
$$
 This is presented as a weaker open form of the preceding poset conjecture and concerns the cross-index after passing to face posets.
record.source_name: Vuong Bui and Hamid Reza Daneshpajouh, “A topological version of Hedetniemi's conjecture for equivariant spaces”, arXiv:2302.06178 (2023).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2302.06178

Status: **open** according to the source (as of February 2023). “However, there are still some interesting open questions around.”

record.title: The Ferrers-poset LE-symmetry conjecture for specified partitions
record.statement: Let $F_\lambda$ be the Ferrers poset associated with a partition $\lambda$, and let $\lambda^t$ be the conjugate partition; the posets $F_\lambda$ and $F_{\lambda^t}$ are isomorphic. A poset is **LE-symmetric** when its Bender–Knuth group acts as the full symmetric group on its set of linear extensions. **The Ferrers-poset LE-symmetry conjecture.** The Ferrers posets $F_\lambda$, and therefore $F_{\lambda^t}$, are LE-symmetric in the following cases: $\lambda=(n,n-2)$ for all $n$; $\lambda=(n,3)$ for $n\not\equiv 2\pmod 4$; and $\lambda=(n,2,2)$ for $n\not\equiv 0\pmod 4$. These are conjectural families motivated by the contrast between LE-cactus and LE-symmetric behavior; the stated cases remain open.
record.source_name: Judy Hsin-Hui Chiang, Anh Trong Nam Hoang, Matthew Kendall, Ryan Lynch, Son Nguyen, Benjamin Przybocki and Janabel Xia, “Bender-Knuth involutions on linear extensions of posets”, arXiv:2302.12425 (2024).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2302.12425

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of February 2023).

record.title: Domination conjecture for neighborhoods in vertex-transitive reflection graphs
record.statement:
Let $H$ be a graph and $x$ a vertex. Define $H_x(k)$ to be the subgraph induced by all vertices at distance at most $k$ from $x$; for vertex-transitive $H$, write this graph as $H(k)$. Say that a graph $H$ **dominates** a graph $H'$ when

$$
t_H(W)^{1/e(H)}\geq t_{H'}(W)^{1/e(H')}
$$

for every graphon $W$.

**Neighborhood domination conjecture.** If $H$ is a vertex-transitive reflection graph with diameter $d$, then $H(\ell)$ dominates $H(k)$ for all $1\leq k\leq \ell\leq d$.

The conjecture proposes a monotonicity principle for domination inequalities among metric neighborhoods in vertex-transitive reflection graphs. The supplied source gives no evidence of a resolution.
record.source_name: David Conlon and Joonkyung Lee, “Domination inequalities and dominating graphs”, arXiv:2303.01997 (2024).

record.title: Coefficient-Length conjecture for triangular diagonal harmonics
record.statement:
Let $\tau$ be a triangular partition, let $\tau'$ denote its conjugate partition, and let $\boldsymbol{\boldsymbol{\basis}}(\mathcal{E}_{\tau}^{(n)})$ denote the coefficient-length of $\mathcal{E}_{\tau}^{(n)}$. Define

$$
\mathcal{A}_{\tau}=\langle \mathcal{E}_{\tau}^{(n)},e_n\rangle.
$$

**Coefficient-Length conjecture.** For all triangular partitions $\tau$,

$$
\boldsymbol{\ell}(\mathcal{E}_{\tau}^{(n)})\leq \min(\boldsymbol{\ell}(\tau),\boldsymbol{\ell}(\tau')),
$$

and $\mathcal{A}_{\tau}$ does not depend on $n$. This proposes uniform length bounds and stability for the associated symmetric-function specialization; the supplied text does not state whether the conjecture is known or open.
record.source_name: François Bergeron, “Triangular Diagonal Harmonics Conjectures”, arXiv:2303.02224 (2023).

record.title: Nonvanishing of the total face color polynomial for bridgeless graphs
record.statement: Let $G$ be a bridgeless connected graph and let $\Gamma$ be a signed ribbon diagram of $G$. For $n$ a positive integer, write $T(\Gamma,n,t)$ for the total face color polynomial. **Total face color polynomial nonvanishing conjecture.** The polynomial $T(\Gamma,n,t)$ is nonzero. This is presented as a stronger form of the cycle double cover conjecture. The theorem immediately preceding it establishes an equivalence between nonvanishing and the existence of a cycle double cover for bridgeless connected trivalent graphs, while the asserted extension to arbitrary bridgeless connected graphs remains open.

record.title: Arbitrary-position rigidity conjecture for bipartized 2-triangulations
record.statement:
Let a reduced bipartized $2$-triangulation be the bipartite graph associated with a reduced $2$-triangulation, and let the vertices be placed at arbitrary distinct points along the parabola.

**Arbitrary-position rigidity conjecture.** Reduced bipartized $2$-triangulations are bases in the bipartite bar-and-joint rigidity matroid of these points.

The generic moment-curve result is known in dimension $2$, and experiments suggest that genericity can be replaced by arbitrary distinct positions; the conjecture asserts this stronger statement.

record.title: The completion conjecture for the $c_2$-invariant of primitive $\phi^4$ graphs
record.statement:
Let $G_1$ and $G_2$ be primitive $\phi^4$ graphs, and let $c_2^{(q)}(G)$ denote the $c_2$-invariant modulo a prime power $q$. Let $\mathcal{P}(G)$ denote the Feynman period. **Completion conjecture.**

$$
\mathcal{P}(G_1)=\mathcal{P}(G_2)\quad\Longrightarrow\quad c_2^{(q)}(G_1)\equiv c_2^{(q)}(G_2)\pmod q
$$

for all prime powers $q$. The paper proves the corresponding completion statement over prime fields using the Martin invariant, while the prime-power formulation remains open in the supplied text.
record.source_name: Erik Panzer and Karen Yeats, “Feynman symmetries of the Martin and c_2 invariants of regular graphs”, arXiv:2304.05299 (2024).

record.title: Extension of the Azevedo–Shumyatsky conciseness conjecture to outer commutator words
record.statement:
Let $w$ be an outer commutator word. Theorems A and B concern, respectively, conciseness of words obtained from lower central or derived words by substitution and conciseness on normal subgroups, where for normal subgroups $N_1,\ldots,N_r$ the set of values is $w\{\mathbf{N}\}$ and the subgroup they generate is $w(\mathbf{N})$.

**Extension of the Azevedo–Shumyatsky conjecture.** Theorems A and B hold for an arbitrary outer commutator word $w$.

The preceding discussion presents this as an extension of the Azevedo–Shumyatsky conjecture. The supplied text does not state whether this extension is proved or remains open.

record.title: Mihail–Vazirani conjecture on rapid mixing of the matroid basis-exchange walk
record.statement: Let $M=(X,\mathcal{I})$ be a matroid, and let its bases be its maximal independent sets. The **base-exchange walk** is the random walk on the bases of $M$ that removes a uniformly chosen element from the current base and then chooses a new base containing the resulting independent set. **Mihail–Vazirani conjecture.** The base-exchange walk converges rapidly. The paper explicitly states that Anari, Liu, Gharan, and Vinzant resolved this conjecture using rapid convergence of the down-up walk on local spectral expanders, so the conjecture is solved.
record.source_name: Roy Gotlib and Tali Kaufman, “No Where to Go But High: A Perspective on High Dimensional Expanders”, arXiv:2304.10106 (2023).

record.title: Finiteness conjecture for the subclass of critically frustrated signed graphs
record.statement:
Let $\mathcal{L}^*(k)$ be the family of irreducible non-decomposable critically $k$-frustrated signed graphs. For each integer $m\leq k$, define $\mathcal{S}^*(k)$ to consist of those elements $(G,\sigma)$ of $\mathcal{L}^*(k)$ such that every critically $m$-frustrated subgraph of $(G,\sigma)$ is non-decomposable.

**Finiteness conjecture.** For every positive integer $k$, the set $\mathcal{S}^*(k)$ is finite.

This is presented as a relaxation of the finiteness conjecture for $\mathcal{L}^*(k)$; its status is not resolved in the source.

record.title: Connectivity conjecture for local dimer dynamics in three dimensions
record.statement: Let $\mathbf{n}$ be a $3$-dimensional shape, and let $\mathcal{D}_3(\mathbb{Q}_{\mathbf{n}}^3)$ denote the graph of dimer configurations on $\mathbb{Q}_{\mathbf{n}}^3$ connected by local moves of length at most $3$. **Connectivity conjecture.** For all $3$-dimensional shapes $\mathbf{n}$, the graph $\mathcal{D}_3(\mathbb{Q}_{\mathbf{n}}^3)$ is connected. This conjecture asks whether local dimer dynamics using moves of length at most $3$ can connect every dimer configuration in every three-dimensional shape. It was posed previously by Milet and Saldanha and reiterated by Freire, Klivans, Milet and Saldanha, and by Chandgotia, Sheffield and Wolfram; its status is not established in the supplied source.

record.title: The weak K-two-threes conjecture for metric matrices
record.statement:
Let $M$ be an $n$-by-$n$ metric matrix, meaning a hollow, symmetric, nonnegative matrix satisfying $m_{jk}\leq m_{ij}+m_{jk}$ for all $1\leq i,j,k\leq n$. Equivalently, $M=M_{\phi G}$ for some weighted graph $G$ and edge-weight function $\phi$. **The weak K-two-threes conjecture.** The matrix $M$ has at most

$$
\left\lfloor \frac{n+1}{3}\right\rfloor
$$

positive eigenvalues. The conjecture is motivated by the preceding characterization of $K_{2,3}$-minor-free graphs and is stated to be tight; its resolution is not provided here.
record.source_name: Jeffrey Cheng, Ian Malcolm Johnson McInnis and Matthew Yee, “Isometric embedding and spectral constraints for weighted graph metrics”, arXiv:2304.13018 (2023).

record.title: Blecher–Knopfmacher's fixed-point inequality for integer partitions
record.statement:
Let $n$ be a positive integer, and let $p(n)$ denote the number of partitions of $n$. A partition $\lambda=(\lambda_1,\ldots,\lambda_j)$ of $n$, written $\lambda\vdash n$, has a fixed point if $\lambda_i=i$ for some index $i$. Let $f(n)$ be the number of partitions of $n$ with a fixed point and $g(n)$ the number without a fixed point. **Blecher–Knopfmacher's conjecture.** For all $n>2$, there are more partitions of $n$ without a fixed point than partitions of $n$ with a fixed point; equivalently, 
$$
g(n)>f(n).
$$
 The paper resolves this open question by proving the inequality and relating fixed points to Frobenius symbols, Dyson's crank, the mex, and other partition statistics.
record.source_name: Brian Hopkins and James A. Sellers, “On Blecher and Knopfmacher's Fixed Points for Integer Partitions”, arXiv:2305.05096 (2023).

record.title: The conjecture on odd girth of rational three-dimensional distance graphs
record.statement: Let $T$ be the set of positive integers under consideration, and let $G(\mathbb{Q}^3,\sqrt{t})$ denote the graph whose vertices are points of $\mathbb{Q}^3$ with adjacency determined by Euclidean distance $\sqrt{t}$. The **odd girth** of a graph is the length of its shortest odd cycle. **The rational-space odd-girth conjecture.** For all $t\in T$, the graph $G(\mathbb{Q}^3,\sqrt{t})$ has odd girth $5$. This is proposed as an analogue in rational three-dimensional space of the paper's earlier conjecture for the corresponding integer setting; the supplied text gives no resolution, so the claim remains open.

record.title: Palindromicity and unimodality conjecture for the EMD numerator polynomials
record.statement:
For positive integers $n$, let $N_n(t)$ be the polynomial defined by the rational generating function

$$
H'_n(t)=\frac{N_n(t)}{(1-t)^{2n}},
$$

where $H'_n(t)=H'_{nn}(t)$ is obtained by differentiating the bivariate generating function for the earth mover's distance on pairs of compositions and evaluating at $z=1$. **Palindromicity and unimodality conjecture.** For all positive integers $n$, the polynomial $N_n(t)$ is palindromic and unimodal. This was the main conjecture of the paper's predecessor and is proved in the present paper.
record.source_name: Rebecca Bourn and William Q. Erickson, “Palindromicity of the numerator of a statistical generating function”, arXiv:2307.02652 (2025).

record.title: The conjecture that all odd cycles are strongly common
record.statement:
Let $W$ be a graphon, meaning a symmetric measurable function $W:[0,1]^2\to[0,1]$, and let $t(H,W)$ denote the homomorphism density of a graph $H$ in $W$. A graph $H$ is **strongly common** if

$$
t(H,W)+t(H,1-W)\geq t(K_2,W)^{e(H)}+t(K_2,1-W)^{e(H)}
$$

for every graphon $W$. **Odd-cycle strong-commonness conjecture.** Every odd cycle is strongly common. Strong commonness implies commonness, and the claim is motivated by the known cases of the triangle and the $5$-cycle; the general assertion remains open.
record.source_name: Natalie Behague, Natasha Morrison and Jonathan A. Noel, “Off-Diagonal Commonality of Graphs via Entropy”, arXiv:2307.03788 (2023).

record.title: Partition regularity of the reciprocal parallelogram pattern
record.statement:
A **finite coloring** of $\mathbb{Q}$ is a coloring using finitely many colors. A pattern is **partition regular over $\mathbb{Q}$** if every finite coloring of $\mathbb{Q}$ admits parameters making all entries of the pattern the same color.

**Reciprocal parallelogram conjecture.** The pattern

$$
\left\{x,\ x+d,\ x+\frac{1}{d},\ x+d+\frac{1}{d}\right\}
$$

is partition regular over $\mathbb{Q}$.

The conjecture asks for a version of a polynomial van der Waerden-type phenomenon allowing negative exponents of $d$. The paper gives no proof and explicitly records the statement as expected to be true.
record.source_name: Ryan Alweiss, “Monochromatic Sums and Products over Q”, arXiv:2307.08901 (2026).

record.title: Existence conjecture for symmetric $[\alpha]$-Hadamard matrices
record.statement:
A symmetric **$[\alpha]$-Hadamard matrix** of order $\zeta$ is a square $\zeta\times\zeta$ matrix with entries in $\{1,-1\}$ that is symmetric and whose distinct-row inner products have absolute value at most $\alpha$. Since ordinary Hadamard matrices are known not to exist in orders not divisible by $4$, the paper introduces these generalized matrices.

**Existence conjecture for symmetric $[\alpha]$-Hadamard matrices.** For every $\alpha\geq 3$, there exist symmetric $[\alpha]$-Hadamard matrices of all orders.

If true, this would extend the constructions based on Hadamard matrices to every order and would make the paper's multipartite Ramsey-number results applicable for all orders $\zeta$.
record.source_name: I Wayan Palton Anuwiksa, Rinovia Simanjuntak and Edy Tri Baskoro, “Multipartite Ramsey numbers of complete bipartite graphs arising from algebraic combinatorial structures”, arXiv:2307.09736 (2023).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2307.09736

Status: **open** according to the source (as of July 2023). “Finally, we conclude by proposing some open problems in Section .”

record.title: Conjecture on the size of bounded-representation additive bases
record.statement:
For a positive integer $m$, let $\mathcal{H}^*_m$ be the set of subsets $A\subseteq\mathbb{Z}_m$ satisfying $1\leq\sigma_A(n)\leq R_m$ for every $n\in\mathbb{Z}_m$, and let

$$
\mathcal{K}_m=\min_{A\in\mathcal{H}^*_m}\{\#A\}.
$$

**Size conjecture for bounded-representation bases.**

$$
\liminf_{m\rightarrow\infty}\frac{\mathcal{K}_m}{\sqrt{3m}}\geq1.
$$

The paper notes that this conjecture is slightly weaker than the preceding mean-representation conjecture, and gives no resolution.
record.source_name: Yuchen Ding and Lilu Zhao, “A new upper bound on Ruzsa's number on the Erdős-Turán conjecture”, arXiv:2307.12311 (2023).

record.title: Merkulov's homology isomorphism conjecture for the truncated graph complex
record.statement:
Let $\mathrm{G}_n$ be the Kontsevich graph complex, with differential $d$, and let $\mathrm{G}^{\mathrm{Me}}_n=\{\Gamma\in\mathrm{G}_n\mid \pi_5\Gamma=\pi_5d\Gamma=0\}$ be Merkulov's truncated graph complex. **Merkulov's conjecture.** The inclusion of dg vector spaces

$$
\mathrm{G}^{\mathrm{Me}}_n\subset\mathrm{G}_n
$$

induces a homology isomorphism

$$
H_k(\mathrm{G}^{\mathrm{Me}}_n)\cong H_k(\mathrm{G}_n)
$$

for all $n$ and $k$. This asserts that the truncated subcomplex captures the full homology of the graph complex; the supplied text gives no evidence of a resolution.
